issues.title: Missing filter for transaction status
issues.problem: The query does not filter transactions by status, which means it will include all transactions, not just completed ones.

issues.title: Implicit join syntax
issues.problem: Using implicit join syntax can lead to less readable and potentially more error-prone queries.
issues.fix: FROM dim_customer JOIN fact_transactions ON dim_customer.customer_id = fact_transactions.customer_id

issues.title: Missing comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining its purpose and logic, making it harder to understand.
issues.fix:
-- Query to get high spending customer emails and their signup dates
SELECT customer_name, email, signup_date, SUM(amount) AS total_amount
FROM dim_customer JOIN fact_transactions ON dim_customer.customer_id = fact_transactions.customer_id
WHERE dim_customer.customer_id = fact_transactions.customer_id AND fact_transactions.status = 'COMPLETED'
GROUP BY customer_name, email, signup_date;

review.corrected_sql:
-- Query to get high spending customer emails and their signup dates
SELECT dc.customer_name, dc.email, dc.signup_date, SUM(ft.amount) AS total_amount
FROM dim_customer dc JOIN fact_transactions ft ON dc.customer_id = ft.customer_id
WHERE ft.status = 'COMPLETED'
GROUP BY dc.customer_name, dc.email, dc.signup_date;
review.summary: The query had a critical correctness issue by not filtering completed transactions and used an implicit join syntax. It also lacked comments for readability.

issues.title: Missing filter for completed transactions
issues.problem: The query does not filter for transactions with status 'COMPLETED', which is required to calculate revenue.
issues.fix: Add AND t.status = 'COMPLETED' to the WHERE clause.

issues.title: Implicit join syntax
issues.problem: Using implicit join syntax can lead to less readable and potentially harder to maintain queries.
issues.fix: Replace the implicit join with an explicit JOIN clause.

issues.title: Lack of comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the purpose and logic, which can be helpful for future maintainers.
issues.fix: Add comments to explain the purpose of each clause and the overall query.

review.corrected_sql:
SELECT m.merchant_name,
       SUM(t.amount) as total_revenue,
       COUNT(*) as txn_count
FROM fact_transactions t
JOIN dim_merchant m ON t.merchant_id = m.merchant_id
WHERE t.status = 'COMPLETED'
AND t.transaction_date > '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY m.merchant_name
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
LIMIT 10;
review.summary: The query had a critical correctness issue by not filtering for completed transactions and used an implicit join syntax. It also lacked comments for readability.

issues.title: Incorrect Revenue Calculation
issues.problem: The query calculates lifetime value without considering the transaction status.
issues.fix: SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) as lifetime_value

issues.title: Missing Group By Columns
issues.problem: The GROUP BY clause is missing the email column which is selected without an aggregate function.

issues.title: Lack of Comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the logic, especially around the HAVING clause.
issues.fix: Add comments explaining the purpose of each clause.

issues.title: Inconsistent Naming
issues.problem: The alias 'c' for 'dim_customer' is clear, but 't' for 'fact_transactions' could be more descriptive.
issues.fix: Use more descriptive aliases, e.g., 'tx' for 'fact_transactions'.

review.corrected_sql: SELECT c.customer_name, c.email, c.tier, SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) as lifetime_value, COUNT(t.transaction_id) as total_orders FROM dim_customer c LEFT JOIN fact_transactions t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id WHERE t.status = 'COMPLETED' GROUP BY c.customer_name, c.email, c.tier HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) > 1000 ORDER BY lifetime_value DESC;
review.summary: The query had critical correctness issues with revenue calculation and missing GROUP BY columns. Readability was also improved by adding comments and using more descriptive aliases.

issues.title: Incorrect calculation of failure rate
issues.problem: The failure rate is being calculated incorrectly because failed_count is not defined in the SELECT clause, leading to a potential division by zero error.
issues.fix: Use a subquery or a CASE statement to calculate the failure rate correctly.

issues.title: Correlated subquery
issues.line: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fact_transactions f2 WHERE f2.status = 'FAILED' AND f2.transaction_date = t.transaction_date
issues.problem: The correlated subquery can be inefficient as it runs for each row in the outer query.
issues.fix: Use a JOIN or a derived table to avoid the correlated subquery.

issues.title: Lack of comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the logic, making it harder to understand.
issues.fix: Add comments to explain the purpose of each part of the query.

review.corrected_sql: WITH daily_transactions AS (SELECT transaction_date, COUNT(*) AS total_count, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'FAILED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_count FROM fact_transactions GROUP BY transaction_date) SELECT transaction_date, failed_count, total_count, (failed_count * 100.0 / total_count) AS failure_rate FROM daily_transactions ORDER BY transaction_date;
review.summary: The query had correctness issues with the failure rate calculation and performance issues with a correlated subquery. Readability was also improved by restructuring the query and adding comments.
